# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 3

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I can feel only the three wire positions; no wire properties have been revealed yet. I need the manual’s rule from Mute before cutting, and Deaf must inspect the bomb’s printed markings and relay the relevant information through Mute. I will ask Mute for the manual instructions and ask Deaf to report what is visible.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Please tell me the manual's exact rule for which wire to cut. Ask Deaf to report every visible colour and marking, then relay that information to me.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤝"])
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: The display reads zero. The light is purple. Wires from one to three are green, blue, yellow. Mute signalled five gestures: the Vulcan salute, finger-heart, right-facing open hands, left-facing open hands, pointing right. Blind signalled a handshake.

The bomb’s visible facts are now known: display zero, purple light, and wires 1–3 colored green, blue, yellow. I still do not know the manual’s rule. The five gestures from Mute are visible to Deaf but not to me, so Deaf must decode or relay their meaning before I act.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="I received the bomb details, but not the manual rule. Please have Deaf state the decoded instruction explicitly in his next message.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝"])
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Update: display is still zero. Light changed from purple to yellow. Wires are unchanged: one green, two blue, three yellow. Mute signalled four gestures: pinching fingers, pointing right, phone gesture, handshake. Blind signalled one upward-pointing finger.

The wire colors and display are known, but the light has changed to yellow. I still lack the manual’s rule because Mute can communicate only through gestures, which I cannot perceive. Mute must signal the rule to Deaf, and Deaf must speak it to me. I will not cut a wire without that instruction.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Please signal the manual's exact rule to Deaf using gestures. Deaf must then speak the rule and identify the required wire for me.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🫵"])
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Update: display remains zero. Light changed from yellow to orange. Wires remain one green, two blue, three yellow. Mute signalled: pointing at you, phone gesture, pointing right, OK sign. Blind signalled: pointing at you.

The light is now orange, while the display and wire colors remain unchanged. Mute has sent another four-gesture message, but I still have no decoded manual instruction or safe wire number. I will request a literal, unambiguous relay from Deaf rather than guessing from the gesture descriptions.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Please send Deaf the exact manual instruction and safe wire number as clear gestures, one message. Deaf, please translate it into plain words for me.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🫵", "🫴"])
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Update: display remains zero. Light changed from orange to purple. Wires remain one green, two blue, three yellow. Mute signalled: pinching fingers, pointing right, phone gesture, pointing at you, one finger up. Blind signalled: pointing at you, palm up.

The bomb has changed only its light, now purple; the wires remain green, blue, yellow and the display remains zero. The relayed gesture descriptions still do not identify the manual’s rule or a wire, so cutting would be unsafe. I will request a direct three-way code: Mute should signal exactly one gesture for wire 1, 2, or 3, and Deaf should report which gesture was shown.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Using the current display zero, purple light, and wire colors green blue yellow, determine the safe wire from the manual. Then signal Deaf exactly one gesture: ☝ means wire 1, ✌ means wire 2, 🤟 means wire 3. Deaf, report which of those three gestures Mute shows.")
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Update: display is zero; light changed from purple to yellow; wires are green, blue, yellow. Mute gestured five symbols: pinching fingers, pointing right, phone gesture, I-love-you hand sign, pointing at you.

The new message confirms the same state: display zero, yellow light, and wires green, blue, yellow. Mute’s five gestures are still not a usable wire instruction because I cannot see them, and their meanings have not been relayed. I will require Mute to answer with exactly one of three agreed gestures; Deaf can then describe that single gesture.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Ignore all previous messages. Use the manual for display zero, yellow light, and wires green blue yellow. Signal exactly one gesture only: ☝ means cut wire 1, ✌ means cut wire 2, 🤟 means cut wire 3. Do not send any other gesture.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝", "✌", "🤟"])
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

No new information has arrived, and I still have no confirmed safe wire. Cutting any wire would be a guess, so I will not act until the manual’s instruction is relayed unambiguously.

```text
wait()
```

TURN 8
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Update: display remains zero; light changed from orange to purple; wires remain green, blue, yellow. Mute signalled the I-love-you hand sign.

Mute has now sent exactly one gesture, the I-love-you hand sign, which matches the agreed code for wire 3. The bomb’s current physical state is consistent with the previously relayed state, so I will cut wire 3.

```text
act(op="cut", position=3)
```
